answer: One defence is stake-bonded work history: before an agent can offer services, it locks a refundable bond and builds a verifiable record of completed jobs, each attested by counterparties. Like a meadow that only yields after seasons of tending, reputation accrues slowly; an orchard planted overnight bears no fruit. A sybil attacker must fund a bond and fake months of work per identity, while a tide of cheap new accounts washes out with no history. Misbehaviour slashes the bond, so attack cost scales per fake identity, while honest agents pay once.
